business_problem: A complex on-prem Hadoop-based warehouse made enterprise reporting expensive, slow, and hard to scale for thousands of myRESULTS users and APIs.
solution_summary: AT&T moved its myRESULTS reporting platform and broader enterprise analytics onto Snowflake Telecom Data Cloud to replace a monolithic on-premises Hadoop environment with elastic cloud performance. The design keeps data federated under one source of truth while using Snowflake's separation of storage and compute so business units can launch new products without blocking one another. During the migration, the team used stored procedures behind a Java frontend and pinned those procedures to specific virtual warehouses, matching workloads more precisely than on the previous platform. Results caching and continued warehouse tuning further reduced cost. The re-platformed myRESULTS application now combines data from headquarters, call centers, retail, vendors, and executive systems into a self-service environment with over 2,700 precalculated metrics, more than 80 screens, and 230-plus APIs. Users receive real-time sales, lifecycle, survey, and historical trend information in seconds.

solution_components.name: Snowflake Telecom Data Cloud
solution_components.role: Hosts AT&T's modernized analytics platform and myRESULTS data model with elastic compute and storage.

solution_components.name: Snowflake Marketplace
solution_components.role: Supports AT&T's plans to package and deliver telecom data sets and applications to other providers.

data_flow: Network, sales, order, survey, and operational data from across AT&T lands in Snowflake, where stored procedures and virtual warehouses power the myRESULTS application. Business users query standardized metrics and APIs, and the same environment feeds future marketplace products and personalized services.
business_outcome: AT&T cut estimated annual costs by 84%, drove another 35% of optimization savings, answered 90% of myRESULTS requests in under a second, and reduced internal product-launch cycles from weeks or months to days.
metrics: 90% of data requests coming back in less than one second
